name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,512

clue.text: Vehicle with endless job when reversing gets driving aid

indicators.note: a word with no end has lost its final letter
reversing a vehicle sends it backwards, so the joined letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
a task is a job

explanation.surface: A driver reversing a van after an endless shift ends up relying on a navigation gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: TASK loses its last letter, then VAN and TAS together are read backwards to give SATNAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav is the satellite navigation device fitted in cars to guide motorists along routes.

clue.text: Completely dispose of host, not half a male with sulky expression

indicators.note: not half means only half of the preceding word survives, the other half dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male
a pout is a sulky pushing out of the lips

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be rid of a party host whose face has fallen into a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: HOST loses its first half, HO, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out something is to eradicate it entirely, as a fire or a rebellion is crushed.

clue.text: Screen set wrongly around Italian writer close to stage

indicators.note: something set wrongly is put in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged
around tells us the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the writer
close here means the end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
Primo Levi was an Italian writer and chemist
the final letter of stage

explanation.surface: A stage set has been badly assembled around an Italian author near the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split so that the writer sits inside them, and the closing letter of stage is tacked on last.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to broadcast it, which is what televising an event means.

clue.text: Decrepit car bachelor abandons in fury

indicators.note: whatever abandons the word walks out of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a banger is British slang for an old, worn-out car
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A single man storms off and leaves his clapped-out car behind in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The B at the front of BANGER is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury and anger are synonyms, both naming a strong feeling of rage or wrath.

clue.text: Novelist dismisses second politician being friendly

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the named letter is removed from the novelist

blocks.note: Kingsley and Martin Amis were both English novelists
S is the abbreviation for second
Vince Cable, former leader of the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A writer sacks a second political figure, yet stays on good terms with them.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIS drops its S to leave AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are cordial and good-natured, which is what friendly conveys.

clue.text: Shame intern disrupted US actor

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An embarrassing intern throws a film actor's day into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Sheen is an American star of Apocalypse Now and The West Wing.

clue.text: Comedy writer with help sent up summaries of work

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: com is the short form of comedy, as in romcom
a pen is a writing instrument
aid means help

explanation.surface: A comic author whose assistant has mocked him produces digests of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mockery but, in a down clue, it turns only the word for help upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, the plural of compendium, are concise collections giving the essence of a larger body.

clue.text: Opening in lower part, it's said

indicators.note: it's said points to how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: the breech is the lower rear part, as of the body or a gun

explanation.surface: Someone reports a gap or hole in the bottom of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or rupture made in a wall or defence, an opening forced through.

clue.text: Like four, say, left close to poverty in a uniform way

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter alone is kept

blocks.note: four is an example of an even number
L is the abbreviation for left
the final letter of poverty

explanation.surface: A family of four is left on the brink of poverty, all treated the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means equally or regularly, without variation, which is doing something uniformly.

clue.text: Claim litre, say, in drink

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for drink

blocks.note: ale is a drink
L is the abbreviation for litre
eg, for example, is what say can mean

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that a litre of something was in their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is to claim it is so.

clue.text: Price set by music company once before opening

blocks.note: pr is a dictionary abbreviation for price
EMI is a British record label
ere is an old word for before; once marks it as archaic

explanation.surface: A record label fixes the ticket cost in advance of a show's first night.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance of a film or play, its opening night.

clue.text: A VIP or tenor primarily at work?

definitions.text: A VIP or tenor primarily at work?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the initial letter alone is used
letters set to work are worked over and rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
the first letter of tenor
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a celebrity singer busy performing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Luciano Pavarotti was a star tenor and certainly a VIP on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the famous Italian operatic tenor, a very important person when performing.

clue.text: Vagrant goes round cast in tatters in area for refugees?

indicators.note: goes round means the first word encircles what follows
something in tatters is torn to pieces, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a tramp is a vagrant
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A homeless wanderer wraps himself in ragged discards in some district.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a transit camp houses displaced people generally, not only refugees.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit camp is a temporary site housing displaced people or refugees while they await relocation.

clue.text: In the audience, forty do well

indicators.note: an audience hears the words, so the clue relies on sound not spelling

blocks.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Forty people in the audience perform well.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding or perform exceptionally, which is doing well.

clue.text: Abroad a certain director encapsulating predicament is without rival

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so one word wraps around the next

blocks.note: un is French for a
sure means certain
a pass is a predicament, as in a pretty pass
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A film director overseas, in a fix, is said to have no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A certain director' looks like one phrase but splits into separate pieces; 'abroad' signals that a is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsurpassed means never exceeded by anyone, so having no equal or competitor.

clue.text: North Yorkshire resort dog, maybe, gets special treatment

blocks.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A dog at a seaside resort in northern England is pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the red carpet means a lavish welcome, from the carpet rolled out for dignitaries.

clue.text: Malign type on ward guarding pair of inmates

indicators.note: a pair is two, so just the first two letters of the next word are kept
a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a hospital ward
the first two letters of inmates

explanation.surface: A wicked figure on a prison or hospital wing keeps watch over two detainees.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is the senior nurse running a ward; she encloses IN as SI...STER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister and malign both describe something evil or harmful in intent.

clue.text: Some painter compromised means of exchange in block?

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An artist's integrity has been damaged by trading in a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'block' means a block of flats, where an entry phone lets residents talk to callers.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is a communication system linking rooms, such as the door entry phone in an apartment building.

clue.text: Son in ground operated in hopeless state

indicators.note: the first in places the son inside the rearranged letters
something ground has been crushed into bits, so the following letters are reformed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son had an operation on the ground in a desperate situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operated in' looks like plain narrative but is the fodder; the final 'in' belongs to it, not to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperation is a condition of despair where one has lost hope, a hopeless state.

clue.text: Gloom opposing counterpart

blocks.note: first meaning: darkness or shade
second meaning: an opposition politician matched to a government minister

explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the opposition party names a 'shadow' for each minister, such as the shadow chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is an area of darkness, and also the opposition spokesperson who mirrors a minister.

clue.text: A king includes four points in response

indicators.note: includes means takes inside, so the points sit within the outer letters

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
the four compass points north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: A monarch embraces four ideas in his reply.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R surround the four compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply or reaction to a question, which is what a response means.

clue.text: Woman with husband put back dye

indicators.note: put back means set in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Anne is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife and husband reapply colour to their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown colouring made from a plant, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Cautious figure beginning to triumph with retro musical

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
retro means looking backwards, so the show's name is read right to left

blocks.note: ten is a number, or figure
the first letter of triumph
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A careful performer's figure starts to win out with an old-fashioned stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means hesitant and provisional, acting carefully without full commitment.

clue.text: Artist after retirement managed Scottish island

indicators.note: retirement is a withdrawal or going back, so the letters are written backwards

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard abbreviation for an artist
ran means managed, as a business

explanation.surface: A painter who has retired ran a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Make light of miserable drama

blocks.note: down means depressed, miserable
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off an unhappy stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to minimise its importance, which is to make light of it.

clue.text: Reviewer right to probe name largely in charge

indicators.note: to probe is to poke inside, so the letter goes into the following word
largely means mostly, so all but the final letter remains

blocks.note: to cite is to name, as a source or example
R is the abbreviation for right
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A reviewer is entitled to investigate a big name in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is a verb here, meaning to mention or quote, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic writes judgements of books, films or plays, which is the job of a reviewer.

clue.text: Kitchen features paid activity, post for cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, and to cook can mean to falsify, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: work is what one is paid to do
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen advert lists features: a paid job and a job vacancy for a chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For cooking' reads as part of the kitchen picture but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Worktops are the flat counter surfaces in a kitchen where food is prepared.

clue.text: Article cut for NI town

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
to trim is to cut

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is shortened for a Northern Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a town north-west of Belfast in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
